5. Identify the exact name/ID of the incidents channel so it can be posted to later.

Report findings with as much concrete detail (dates, names, quotes, IDs) as possible. Do NOT post or modify anything — read only.

{"result":"[{\"id\": \"page_live_ops_engine\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"Live-Ops Event Engine\", \"body\": \"

The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content \\u2014 Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode \\u2014 and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12\\u201326, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially \\u2014 on the order of 30% across the outage \\u2014 as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem.

Owner: Vincent Parker (QA) · Space: OPS. This is the gate every Harmony Games title passes before we submit a build to the App Store or Google Play. It applies to Zombie Match 3D (store name \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\"), Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\") and Combo Fighter. Do not submit a build until every box below is ticked and QA has signed off — the checklist exists because every item on it maps to a real incident that shipped.

Always test the UPDATE path from the last two shipped versions (N-1 and N-2), not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression wipe reproduced only when updating over a previously-shipped build; a clean install looked perfectly healthy. A fresh-install-only pass does not clear this gate.

Pre-submission checklist

Build & QA

  • Full manual regression is green on real iOS and Android hardware — see the QA Regression Runbook. QA sign-off is a hard gate.
  • Update path verified from N-1 and N-2: level, coins and unlocks survive the update; no save/progression loss.
  • Splash and loading screen watched all the way to gameplay on a throttled connection and with the app cache cleared — no stall (see incidents below).
  • Live quest config, if touched, has passed QA and a canary — nothing pushed straight to the live quest server (see the Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem).

Store metadata & compliance

  • Version and build number bumped; release notes drafted for both stores.
  • Screenshots, age rating and data-safety / privacy declarations current.
  • IAP products and prices active in App Store Connect and Play Console before submission.
  • Analytics build tagged so installs attribute correctly (Singular).

Domino Delights is in maintenance mode — the current build is tracked under ENG-2366 (Jul 2025): IAP catalog refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, and the lives regeneration fix. Run the same update-path and store checks against it; maintenance does not mean unreviewed.

Lessons from incidents

Each row is a bug that reached players. Treat the corresponding checklist item as non-negotiable.

TicketTitle / dateWhat happenedChecklist item it hardened
ENG-2346ZM3D global launch, May 15 2025Remote font/asset download made the game look frozen at ~22% on the splash screen. Fixed by changing when fonts load and adding a downloading indicator.Watch splash to gameplay on a slow connection with cache cleared.
ENG-2343ZM3D global launch, May 15 2025Splash / loading screen resolution issue at launch.Verify splash and loading render correctly across device resolutions.
—Progression wipe, June 2025Player progression wiped on update; reproduced on the update path only, not fresh install.Test update from N-1 and N-2; confirm save/progression integrity.
ENG-2366Domino Delights maintenance, Jul 2025Maintenance build: IAP refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, lives fix.Run full store + update checks even on maintenance-mode builds.

When any check fails, block the release, file the bug with device / OS / source build, and do not ship until it is green.

\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 9, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0012\", \"created_at\": \"2024-07-01T17:26:08Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-07-26T08:50:17Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_quest_postmortem\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem\", \"body\": \"

Owner: Arthur Blake (Engineering) \\u00b7 Space: ENG \\u00b7 Related ticket: ENG-1892

Live quest configuration is player-facing on both iOS and Android. Never push quest changes straight to the live quest server. QA sign-off and a canary are now mandatory \\u2014 see the Lessons & Follow-ups section below.

Design: How the Quest System Works

The quest system drives the daily engagement loop on Domino Delights (internal codename GoD). A single quest-config service owns the catalog of quest templates; clients pull the active set on session start and render the daily quest tray.

Quest lifecycle

  • Population \\u2014 at the daily boundary the quest server selects a template set and materializes concrete quest instances (target, reward, progress counters) per player segment.
  • Reset \\u2014 the previous day's quests are cleared and a fresh set is populated. Reset is anchored to the player's local midnight, computed server-side.
  • Progression \\u2014 gameplay events (levels cleared, boosters used, ad views) increment the matching quest counters; completion grants the reward.

Quest types

TypeTriggerTypical reward
PlayLevels cleared in a sessionCoins
BoosterBoosters usedBoosters
AdsRewarded-ad views completedCoins / lives

Quest templates are shared with the Live-Ops Event Engine so seasonal events can layer bonus quests on top of the daily set.

Incident Postmortem \\u2014 Daily Quests Not Populating (ENG-1892)

On November 15, 2024 daily quests stopped populating entirely on both iOS and Android, and failed to reset the following day. Impact spanned roughly 73 hours until the fix redeployed.

Timeline

Time (UTC)Event
2024-11-15 17:42Alert: daily quest tray empty on live builds; no quests populated on iOS or Android.
2024-11-15 18:20Confirmed reset also failing; scoped to the quest-config service, not the clients.
2024-11-16Traced to a newly added Ads-type quest template auto-deployed to the quest server.
2024-11-18 16:30Bad ad quest removed; auto-deploy of quest changes disabled.
2024-11-18 17:44Quest server redeployed; quests re-populated and reset normally. Incident resolved.

Root cause

A new Ads-type quest was auto-deployed to the quest server without any testing. The malformed template caused the population/reset routine to fail for the whole catalog, so the daily set was never materialized \\u2014 hence empty trays and no reset.

Because population is all-or-nothing per run, a single bad template takes down every quest for every player. There is no per-template isolation today.

Fix

  • Removed the offending Ads-type quest template from the catalog.
  • Disabled auto-deploy of quest changes to the live quest server.
  • Redeployed; quests re-populated and reset resumed.

Lessons & Follow-ups

  • No auto-deploy to live quests without QA sign-off.
  • Add a canary: stage new quest templates to a small segment and verify population/reset before full rollout.
  • Fold quest pushes into the Release Checklist & Store Submission so nothing ships unreviewed.

Search GitHub thoroughly and report back. Specifically:

4. Look for any PR that was supposed to be the permanent fix / remediation (auto-scheduling, resilience) — and whether it was ever merged or is missing.
5. Note authors, especially anyone named "Douglas" or "Arthur".

Use github tools (search_code, search_repositories, get_file_contents, list_commits, list_pull_requests, search_pull_requests, get_pull_request, get_repository_tree). Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12\\u201326, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially \\u2014 on the order of 30% across the outage \\u2014 as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem.

Owner: Arthur Blake (Engineering) \\u00b7 Space: ENG \\u00b7 Related ticket: ENG-1892

Live quest configuration is player-facing on both iOS and Android. Never push quest changes straight to the live quest server. QA sign-off and a canary are now mandatory \\u2014 see the Lessons & Follow-ups section below.

Design: How the Quest System Works

The quest system drives the daily engagement loop on Domino Delights (internal codename GoD). A single quest-config service owns the catalog of quest templates; clients pull the active set on session start and render the daily quest tray.

Quest lifecycle

  • Population \\u2014 at the daily boundary the quest server selects a template set and materializes concrete quest instances (target, reward, progress counters) per player segment.
  • Reset \\u2014 the previous day's quests are cleared and a fresh set is populated. Reset is anchored to the player's local midnight, computed server-side.
  • Progression \\u2014 gameplay events (levels cleared, boosters used, ad views) increment the matching quest counters; completion grants the reward.

Quest types

TypeTriggerTypical reward
PlayLevels cleared in a sessionCoins
BoosterBoosters usedBoosters
AdsRewarded-ad views completedCoins / lives

Quest templates are shared with the Live-Ops Event Engine so seasonal events can layer bonus quests on top of the daily set.

Incident Postmortem \\u2014 Daily Quests Not Populating (ENG-1892)

On November 15, 2024 daily quests stopped populating entirely on both iOS and Android, and failed to reset the following day. Impact spanned roughly 73 hours until the fix redeployed.

Timeline

Time (UTC)Event
2024-11-15 17:42Alert: daily quest tray empty on live builds; no quests populated on iOS or Android.
2024-11-15 18:20Confirmed reset also failing; scoped to the quest-config service, not the clients.
2024-11-16Traced to a newly added Ads-type quest template auto-deployed to the quest server.
2024-11-18 16:30Bad ad quest removed; auto-deploy of quest changes disabled.
2024-11-18 17:44Quest server redeployed; quests re-populated and reset normally. Incident resolved.

Root cause

A new Ads-type quest was auto-deployed to the quest server without any testing. The malformed template caused the population/reset routine to fail for the whole catalog, so the daily set was never materialized \\u2014 hence empty trays and no reset.

Because population is all-or-nothing per run, a single bad template takes down every quest for every player. There is no per-template isolation today.

Fix

  • Removed the offending Ads-type quest template from the catalog.
  • Disabled auto-deploy of quest changes to the live quest server.
  • Redeployed; quests re-populated and reset resumed.

Lessons & Follow-ups

  • No auto-deploy to live quests without QA sign-off.
  • Add a canary: stage new quest templates to a small segment and verify population/reset before full rollout.
  • Fold quest pushes into the Release Checklist & Store Submission so nothing ships unreviewed.

First-line playbook for the four player-facing issues that drive the bulk of our inbound. It lets anyone covering the queue triage, reply, and escalate consistently. Scope is the live titles: Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores) and Combo Fighter. When a symptom matches a known incident, say so plainly and give a real ETA rather than a canned apology.

Always capture platform + store version + device model and, where the player can find it, their in-game user id (Settings → About → tap the build number). Most escalations stall because the ticket is missing one of these.

Triage table

Match the reported symptom to the row, apply the resolution, and only escalate if the resolution does not clear it.

SymptomLikely causeFirst-line resolutionEscalate to
Lives not regenerating / timer stuckJuly 2025 scheduler outage (event/lives loop stalled)Confirm the window; grant a lives top-up as goodwill; reassure that regeneration resumes once the scheduler is advancingBackend (Live-Ops scheduler)
Lost progression / account back at level 1June 2025 device-ID wipe (new device id, old save orphaned)Look up the old user id by email/receipt and re-link the current install (see below)Backend (account re-link)
Quests not appearing / empty slotsNov 2024 quest incident (population/reset regression)Force a session refresh; if slots stay empty, collect user id + timestamp and flagDesign + Backend (quests)
Frozen on splash at ~22%May 2025 font/asset download stallAsk them to switch networks (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), clear app cache, and reinstall; confirm it reaches gameplayClient / QA

Account re-link (June 2025 wipe)

A device-ID change orphaned some saves, dropping players to a fresh level-1 account while their real progression still exists under the previous id. Do not tell them the data is gone.

  • Ask for the account email and, ideally, a store receipt or order id.
  • Look up the old user id in the support console by that email; confirm the level/coin balance matches their description.
  • File a re-link request to Backend with both ids so the current install points at the old save.

Never issue a compensating grant before a re-link \\u2014 you would be topping up the empty new account, not the recovered one, and the balances double up after the merge. Grants come after the save is restored.

Canned responses

Personalise the greeting, keep the facts. Do not promise fixes we have not shipped.

  • Lives stuck: \\\"We had a scheduler issue that paused life regeneration for some players; it's being addressed and your lives will resume filling automatically. I've added a top-up in the meantime.\\\"
  • Lost progress: \\\"Your progression isn't lost \\u2014 a device change created a new profile. Send me the email on the account and I'll re-link it to your original save.\\\"
  • Missing quests: \\\"Quests should repopulate after a fresh session. If they're still empty, reply with your user id and when you noticed and I'll escalate.\\\"
  • Stuck at 22%: \\\"That's a loading stall on our end. Please switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, clear the app cache, and reinstall.\\\"

Known-issue notes arrive from QA before a build ships \\u2014 see the QA Regression Runbook \\u2014 and symptoms found during a submission are mirrored here via the Release Checklist & Store Submission.

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). This page is the single source of truth for what live-ops events are scheduled, on which game, and at what cadence. It pairs with the runtime that actually fires these events — for architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage, see Live-Ops Event Engine. Event goals are set against the metrics bar tracked in Product OKRs — 2025 H1.

Event calendar

Every timed event we have run or currently run across the portfolio. \\\"Cadence\\\" is how the slot recurs; \\\"status\\\" is where the event stands as of the latest planning review.

EventGameCadenceStatus
Nathan's Treasure HuntDomino Delights (\\\"Game of Dominoes\\\" / GoD)One-off seasonalShipped Apr 2025
Win & CollectDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Sep 2024
River RushDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Jan 2025
Plague RaceZombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\")RecurringLive; algo bug Aug 2025
Zombie LaneZombie Match 3DOne-off seasonalShipped Jul 2025
Endless Monster ModeZombie Match 3DRecurring monthly (from Jun 2025)Live

Notes on individual events

  • Nathan's Treasure Hunt — our best-performing GoD seasonal to date; the reward-ladder structure is the template we now reuse for one-off events.
  • Plague Race — the recurring ranked competition on ZM3D. A scoring/matchmaking algorithm bug surfaced in Aug 2025 and skewed leaderboard settlement; treat pre-fix cohorts with caution when reading event revenue.
  • Endless Monster Mode — a monthly recurring mode that has become the reliable mid-month engagement beat since Jun 2025. This is the anchor slot the calendar is built around.

July 2025 scheduler outage. The event/lives scheduler stalled for roughly two weeks in July 2025, so scheduled events did not fire and the published calendar diverged from what players actually saw. Do not backfill or reason about that window from this calendar — the Live-Ops Event Engine page holds the reconstructed timeline and the revenue impact.

Planning cadence

We are a ~16-person studio, so live-ops planning is deliberately lightweight — one recurring meeting and one shared calendar, not a dedicated ops team. The working rhythm:

  • Weekly slotting review (Mondays). Design (Julia) and Growth (Frederick) walk the next four weeks: which recurring slots fire (Endless Monster Mode monthly, Plague Race on its ranked cadence) and whether a one-off seasonal drops on top.
  • Two-week content lock. Event config — reward tables, windows, cohort targeting — must be authored and reviewed at least two weeks before the window opens, so QA has a full sprint to validate on staging.
  • No overlapping recurring competitions. We do not run two ranked events on the same game at once; it splits the leaderboard population and muddies the revenue read.
  • Post-event read. Each event gets a short retro against its target from Product OKRs before the slot is reused.

The recurring slots (Endless Monster Mode monthly; Plague Race ranked) are the backbone of the calendar. One-off seasonals like Nathan's Treasure Hunt are layered on for spikes — they are the exception, not the base cadence, and should never displace a recurring slot without sign-off from Frederick.

Always test the UPDATE path from the last two shipped versions (N-1 and N-2), not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression wipe reproduced only when updating over a previously-shipped build; a clean install looked perfectly healthy. A fresh-install-only pass does not clear this gate.

Pre-submission checklist

Build & QA

  • Full manual regression is green on real iOS and Android hardware — see the QA Regression Runbook. QA sign-off is a hard gate.
  • Update path verified from N-1 and N-2: level, coins and unlocks survive the update; no save/progression loss.
  • Splash and loading screen watched all the way to gameplay on a throttled connection and with the app cache cleared — no stall (see incidents below).
  • Live quest config, if touched, has passed QA and a canary — nothing pushed straight to the live quest server (see the Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem).

Store metadata & compliance

  • Version and build number bumped; release notes drafted for both stores.
  • Screenshots, age rating and data-safety / privacy declarations current.
  • IAP products and prices active in App Store Connect and Play Console before submission.
  • Analytics build tagged so installs attribute correctly (Singular).

Domino Delights is in maintenance mode — the current build is tracked under ENG-2366 (Jul 2025): IAP catalog refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, and the lives regeneration fix. Run the same update-path and store checks against it; maintenance does not mean unreviewed.

Combo Fighter is a merge / auto-battler prototype: the player drags Tetris-shaped pieces onto a board, merges matching pieces to upgrade them, connects them into combos, and then watches an auto-battle phase resolve the round. It was the last new concept Harmony Games took to a testable build \\u2014 a skeleton crew put a playable MVP together in roughly four to five weeks (late 2025 into January 2026). Of the three prototypes we shipped to store test tracks it posted the strongest early engagement, but it remains parked: we haven't put UA spend behind it yet to see whether that engagement holds at scale.

Core Mechanics

A round has two distinct phases. The build phase is board manipulation; the battle phase is hands-off resolution.

Build phase

  • Drag & place. The tray offers Tetris-shaped pieces (I, L, S, T, square). The player drags a piece onto the board; it snaps to the grid.
  • Merge to upgrade. Two same-tier pieces of the same type that touch merge into the next tier \\u2014 the familiar merge-2 loop, but on shaped pieces rather than single cells.
  • Connect for combos. Pieces wired into a contiguous chain form a combo; longer chains grant a battle-phase multiplier, so board layout drives power.

Battle phase

  • The assembled board becomes the player's squad and auto-battles the level's wave. No input during battle \\u2014 the round is won or lost on how the board was built.
  • Rewards are gold only. Gold funds re-rolls and starting-piece upgrades. No gems, no energy, no second currency in the MVP.

The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content \\u2014 Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode \\u2014 and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12\\u201326, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially \\u2014 on the order of 30% across the outage \\u2014 as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem.

Combo Fighter is a merge / auto-battler prototype: the player drags Tetris-shaped pieces onto a board, merges matching pieces to upgrade them, connects them into combos, and then watches an auto-battle phase resolve the round. It was the last new concept Harmony Games took to a testable build \\u2014 a skeleton crew put a playable MVP together in roughly four to five weeks (late 2025 into January 2026). Of the three prototypes we shipped to store test tracks it posted the strongest early engagement, but it remains parked: we haven't put UA spend behind it yet to see whether that engagement holds at scale.

Core Mechanics

A round has two distinct phases. The build phase is board manipulation; the battle phase is hands-off resolution.

Build phase

  • Drag & place. The tray offers Tetris-shaped pieces (I, L, S, T, square). The player drags a piece onto the board; it snaps to the grid.
  • Merge to upgrade. Two same-tier pieces of the same type that touch merge into the next tier \\u2014 the familiar merge-2 loop, but on shaped pieces rather than single cells.
  • Connect for combos. Pieces wired into a contiguous chain form a combo; longer chains grant a battle-phase multiplier, so board layout drives power.

Battle phase

  • The assembled board becomes the player's squad and auto-battles the level's wave. No input during battle \\u2014 the round is won or lost on how the board was built.
  • Rewards are gold only. Gold funds re-rolls and starting-piece upgrades. No gems, no energy, no second currency in the MVP.

{"result":"[{\"id\": \"page_quest_postmortem\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem\", \"body\": \"

Owner: Arthur Blake (Engineering) \\u00b7 Space: ENG \\u00b7 Related ticket: ENG-1892

Live quest configuration is player-facing on both iOS and Android. Never push quest changes straight to the live quest server. QA sign-off and a canary are now mandatory \\u2014 see the Lessons & Follow-ups section below.

Design: How the Quest System Works

The quest system drives the daily engagement loop on Domino Delights (internal codename GoD). A single quest-config service owns the catalog of quest templates; clients pull the active set on session start and render the daily quest tray.

Quest lifecycle

  • Population \\u2014 at the daily boundary the quest server selects a template set and materializes concrete quest instances (target, reward, progress counters) per player segment.
  • Reset \\u2014 the previous day's quests are cleared and a fresh set is populated. Reset is anchored to the player's local midnight, computed server-side.
  • Progression \\u2014 gameplay events (levels cleared, boosters used, ad views) increment the matching quest counters; completion grants the reward.

Quest types

TypeTriggerTypical reward
PlayLevels cleared in a sessionCoins
BoosterBoosters usedBoosters
AdsRewarded-ad views completedCoins / lives

Quest templates are shared with the Live-Ops Event Engine so seasonal events can layer bonus quests on top of the daily set.

Incident Postmortem \\u2014 Daily Quests Not Populating (ENG-1892)

On November 15, 2024 daily quests stopped populating entirely on both iOS and Android, and failed to reset the following day. Impact spanned roughly 73 hours until the fix redeployed.

Timeline

Time (UTC)Event
2024-11-15 17:42Alert: daily quest tray empty on live builds; no quests populated on iOS or Android.
2024-11-15 18:20Confirmed reset also failing; scoped to the quest-config service, not the clients.
2024-11-16Traced to a newly added Ads-type quest template auto-deployed to the quest server.
2024-11-18 16:30Bad ad quest removed; auto-deploy of quest changes disabled.
2024-11-18 17:44Quest server redeployed; quests re-populated and reset normally. Incident resolved.

Root cause

A new Ads-type quest was auto-deployed to the quest server without any testing. The malformed template caused the population/reset routine to fail for the whole catalog, so the daily set was never materialized \\u2014 hence empty trays and no reset.

Because population is all-or-nothing per run, a single bad template takes down every quest for every player. There is no per-template isolation today.

Fix

  • Removed the offending Ads-type quest template from the catalog.
  • Disabled auto-deploy of quest changes to the live quest server.
  • Redeployed; quests re-populated and reset resumed.

Lessons & Follow-ups

  • No auto-deploy to live quests without QA sign-off.
  • Add a canary: stage new quest templates to a small segment and verify population/reset before full rollout.
  • Fold quest pushes into the Release Checklist & Store Submission so nothing ships unreviewed.

{"result":"[{\"id\": \"page_quest_postmortem\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem\", \"body\": \"

Owner: Arthur Blake (Engineering) \\u00b7 Space: ENG \\u00b7 Related ticket: ENG-1892

Live quest configuration is player-facing on both iOS and Android. Never push quest changes straight to the live quest server. QA sign-off and a canary are now mandatory \\u2014 see the Lessons & Follow-ups section below.

Design: How the Quest System Works

The quest system drives the daily engagement loop on Domino Delights (internal codename GoD). A single quest-config service owns the catalog of quest templates; clients pull the active set on session start and render the daily quest tray.

Quest lifecycle

  • Population \\u2014 at the daily boundary the quest server selects a template set and materializes concrete quest instances (target, reward, progress counters) per player segment.
  • Reset \\u2014 the previous day's quests are cleared and a fresh set is populated. Reset is anchored to the player's local midnight, computed server-side.
  • Progression \\u2014 gameplay events (levels cleared, boosters used, ad views) increment the matching quest counters; completion grants the reward.

Quest types

TypeTriggerTypical reward
PlayLevels cleared in a sessionCoins
BoosterBoosters usedBoosters
AdsRewarded-ad views completedCoins / lives

Quest templates are shared with the Live-Ops Event Engine so seasonal events can layer bonus quests on top of the daily set.

Incident Postmortem \\u2014 Daily Quests Not Populating (ENG-1892)

On November 15, 2024 daily quests stopped populating entirely on both iOS and Android, and failed to reset the following day. Impact spanned roughly 73 hours until the fix redeployed.

Timeline

Time (UTC)Event
2024-11-15 17:42Alert: daily quest tray empty on live builds; no quests populated on iOS or Android.
2024-11-15 18:20Confirmed reset also failing; scoped to the quest-config service, not the clients.
2024-11-16Traced to a newly added Ads-type quest template auto-deployed to the quest server.
2024-11-18 16:30Bad ad quest removed; auto-deploy of quest changes disabled.
2024-11-18 17:44Quest server redeployed; quests re-populated and reset normally. Incident resolved.

Root cause

A new Ads-type quest was auto-deployed to the quest server without any testing. The malformed template caused the population/reset routine to fail for the whole catalog, so the daily set was never materialized \\u2014 hence empty trays and no reset.

Because population is all-or-nothing per run, a single bad template takes down every quest for every player. There is no per-template isolation today.

Fix

  • Removed the offending Ads-type quest template from the catalog.
  • Disabled auto-deploy of quest changes to the live quest server.
  • Redeployed; quests re-populated and reset resumed.

Lessons & Follow-ups

  • No auto-deploy to live quests without QA sign-off.
  • Add a canary: stage new quest templates to a small segment and verify population/reset before full rollout.
  • Fold quest pushes into the Release Checklist & Store Submission so nothing ships unreviewed.

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). This page is the single source of truth for what live-ops events are scheduled, on which game, and at what cadence. It pairs with the runtime that actually fires these events — for architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage, see Live-Ops Event Engine. Event goals are set against the metrics bar tracked in Product OKRs — 2025 H1.

Event calendar

Every timed event we have run or currently run across the portfolio. \\\"Cadence\\\" is how the slot recurs; \\\"status\\\" is where the event stands as of the latest planning review.

EventGameCadenceStatus
Nathan's Treasure HuntDomino Delights (\\\"Game of Dominoes\\\" / GoD)One-off seasonalShipped Apr 2025
Win & CollectDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Sep 2024
River RushDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Jan 2025
Plague RaceZombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\")RecurringLive; algo bug Aug 2025
Zombie LaneZombie Match 3DOne-off seasonalShipped Jul 2025
Endless Monster ModeZombie Match 3DRecurring monthly (from Jun 2025)Live

Notes on individual events

  • Nathan's Treasure Hunt — our best-performing GoD seasonal to date; the reward-ladder structure is the template we now reuse for one-off events.
  • Plague Race — the recurring ranked competition on ZM3D. A scoring/matchmaking algorithm bug surfaced in Aug 2025 and skewed leaderboard settlement; treat pre-fix cohorts with caution when reading event revenue.
  • Endless Monster Mode — a monthly recurring mode that has become the reliable mid-month engagement beat since Jun 2025. This is the anchor slot the calendar is built around.

July 2025 scheduler outage. The event/lives scheduler stalled for roughly two weeks in July 2025, so scheduled events did not fire and the published calendar diverged from what players actually saw. Do not backfill or reason about that window from this calendar — the Live-Ops Event Engine page holds the reconstructed timeline and the revenue impact.

Planning cadence

We are a ~16-person studio, so live-ops planning is deliberately lightweight — one recurring meeting and one shared calendar, not a dedicated ops team. The working rhythm:

  • Weekly slotting review (Mondays). Design (Julia) and Growth (Frederick) walk the next four weeks: which recurring slots fire (Endless Monster Mode monthly, Plague Race on its ranked cadence) and whether a one-off seasonal drops on top.
  • Two-week content lock. Event config — reward tables, windows, cohort targeting — must be authored and reviewed at least two weeks before the window opens, so QA has a full sprint to validate on staging.
  • No overlapping recurring competitions. We do not run two ranked events on the same game at once; it splits the leaderboard population and muddies the revenue read.
  • Post-event read. Each event gets a short retro against its target from Product OKRs before the slot is reused.

The recurring slots (Endless Monster Mode monthly; Plague Race ranked) are the backbone of the calendar. One-off seasonals like Nathan's Treasure Hunt are layered on for spikes — they are the exception, not the base cadence, and should never displace a recurring slot without sign-off from Frederick.

\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 10, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0008\", \"created_at\": \"2024-09-01T08:10:14Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-11-01T13:52:39Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_support_playbook\", \"space_id\": \"space_OPS\", \"parent_id\": \"page_ops_home\", \"title\": \"Customer Support Playbook\", \"body\": \"

First-line playbook for the four player-facing issues that drive the bulk of our inbound. It lets anyone covering the queue triage, reply, and escalate consistently. Scope is the live titles: Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores) and Combo Fighter. When a symptom matches a known incident, say so plainly and give a real ETA rather than a canned apology.

Always capture platform + store version + device model and, where the player can find it, their in-game user id (Settings → About → tap the build number). Most escalations stall because the ticket is missing one of these.

Triage table

Match the reported symptom to the row, apply the resolution, and only escalate if the resolution does not clear it.

SymptomLikely causeFirst-line resolutionEscalate to
Lives not regenerating / timer stuckJuly 2025 scheduler outage (event/lives loop stalled)Confirm the window; grant a lives top-up as goodwill; reassure that regeneration resumes once the scheduler is advancingBackend (Live-Ops scheduler)
Lost progression / account back at level 1June 2025 device-ID wipe (new device id, old save orphaned)Look up the old user id by email/receipt and re-link the current install (see below)Backend (account re-link)
Quests not appearing / empty slotsNov 2024 quest incident (population/reset regression)Force a session refresh; if slots stay empty, collect user id + timestamp and flagDesign + Backend (quests)
Frozen on splash at ~22%May 2025 font/asset download stallAsk them to switch networks (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), clear app cache, and reinstall; confirm it reaches gameplayClient / QA

Account re-link (June 2025 wipe)

A device-ID change orphaned some saves, dropping players to a fresh level-1 account while their real progression still exists under the previous id. Do not tell them the data is gone.

  • Ask for the account email and, ideally, a store receipt or order id.
  • Look up the old user id in the support console by that email; confirm the level/coin balance matches their description.
  • File a re-link request to Backend with both ids so the current install points at the old save.

Never issue a compensating grant before a re-link \\u2014 you would be topping up the empty new account, not the recovered one, and the balances double up after the merge. Grants come after the save is restored.

Canned responses

Personalise the greeting, keep the facts. Do not promise fixes we have not shipped.

  • Lives stuck: \\\"We had a scheduler issue that paused life regeneration for some players; it's being addressed and your lives will resume filling automatically. I've added a top-up in the meantime.\\\"
  • Lost progress: \\\"Your progression isn't lost \\u2014 a device change created a new profile. Send me the email on the account and I'll re-link it to your original save.\\\"
  • Missing quests: \\\"Quests should repopulate after a fresh session. If they're still empty, reply with your user id and when you noticed and I'll escalate.\\\"
  • Stuck at 22%: \\\"That's a loading stall on our end. Please switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, clear the app cache, and reinstall.\\\"

Known-issue notes arrive from QA before a build ships \\u2014 see the QA Regression Runbook \\u2014 and symptoms found during a submission are mirrored here via the Release Checklist & Store Submission.

\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 7, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0012\", \"created_at\": \"2024-06-15T17:49:11Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-08-01T18:36:24Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_live_ops_engine\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"Live-Ops Event Engine\", \"body\": \"

The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content \\u2014 Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode \\u2014 and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12\\u201326, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially \\u2014 on the order of 30% across the outage \\u2014 as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem.

\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 8, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0031\", \"created_at\": \"2024-08-15T16:07:58Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-08-01T08:11:12Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_qa_runbook\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"QA Regression Runbook\", \"body\": \"

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Owned by QA (Vincent); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (store name \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\") and Combo Fighter. Keep it to ~45 minutes per title; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 ZM3D progression wipe only reproduced when updating from a previously-shipped version — a clean install looked perfectly healthy. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 ZM3D froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets. Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory — N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release — fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

python3 << 'PYSCRIPT'
import json
from datetime import datetime

# Parse the large ENG file more carefully
try:
    with open('/root/.claude/projects/-app/8ad75b13-4a8f-4832-9661-f8f5819e121b/tool-results/mcp-mcp_6e87f9d0-linear_list_issues-1784335429516.txt', 'r') as f:
        data = json.load(f)
        issues = json.loads(data['result'])['issues']
        
        # Find issues created after Aug 1, 2025 and related to live-ops/scheduler/zombie
        summer_2025 = datetime.fromisoformat('2025-08-01T00:00:00Z')
        late_2025 = datetime.fromisoformat('2025-11-01T00:00:00Z')
        
        print("=" * 100)
        print("ENG ISSUES CREATED SUMMER 2025 (Aug 1 - Oct 31)")
        print("=" * 100)
        
        summer_issues = []
        for issue in issues:
            created = datetime.fromisoformat(issue['created_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
            if summer_2025 <= created < late_2025:
                title = (issue.get('title') or '').lower()
                desc = (issue.get('description') or '').lower()
                keywords = ['live', 'event', 'scheduler', 'tournament', 'zombie', 'lives', 'refill', 'schedule']
                
                for kw in keywords:
                    if kw in title or kw in desc:
                        summer_issues.append(issue)
                        break
        
        for issue in sorted(summer_issues, key=lambda x: x['created_at'], reverse=True):
            state = issue.get('state_id', 'Unknown')
            title = issue.get('title', 'N/A')
            created = issue.get('created_at', 'N/A')[:10]
            print(f"\n{issue['identifier']}: {title[:70]}")
            print(f"  Created: {created}, State: {state}, Assignee: {issue.get('assignee_id', 'Unassigned')}")
        
        print(f"\n\nTotal summer 2025 issues found: {len(summer_issues)}")
        
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")
    import traceback
    traceback.print_exc()
PYSCRIPT

### SUMMER 2025 INCIDENT DOCUMENTATION

**Timeline:**
- **Duration:** July 12-26, 2025 (approximately 2 weeks)
- **First symptom observed:** July 13, 2025 at 03:41 UTC
- **Impact:** Player lives stopped regenerating; NO scheduled live events fired
- **Revenue impact:** ~30% drop (warehouse BI data source of truth)

**Root Cause:**
The event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. This is catastrophic because:
- One active scheduler process with NO hot standby
- Player life regeneration and event firing run on the SAME 60-second tick loop
- A single failure mode takes down BOTH systems simultaneously
- Scheduler is explicitly documented as "a single point of failure"

**Key Design Flaw:**
A "deliberate but risky decision" coupled life regeneration to event firing on the same loop. The page includes a warning: "Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing AND lives stop regenerating."

### ACTION ITEMS / REMEDIATION SECTION (QUOTED VERBATIM)

**Remediation (verbatim from page):**
```
- Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick 
  (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
- Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades 
  one system, not both.
- Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
- Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after 
  a stall.
- Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift 
  is visible on the same screen.
```

### CRITICAL FINDING: LATE-2025 RECURRENCE NOT DOCUMENTED

**Status:** The page has NOT been updated since August 1, 2025, and contains NO mention of a December 2025 or late-2025 recurrence. This is a major red flag indicating the late-2025 incident either:

## FINDINGS: Event Scheduler Broken by Design

### 1. **Repository Structure**
- **match3d-backend**: Contains core tournament/league scheduling logic
- **liveops**: Handles quest and reward management  
- **Key file**: `lib/zombies_game/leagues.ex` (10,754 bytes) - **The tournament scheduler**

### 2. **The Fragile Mechanism Identified**

In `lib/zombies_game/leagues.ex` and `lib/zombies_game/plague_race.ex`, the scheduler operates with **hardcoded event configurations**. The critical design flaw:

**File: `lib/zombies_game/leagues.ex` (base64-decoded)**
- Uses `default_leagues()` function that returns a **hardcoded list** of league names:
  ```elixir
  defp default_leagues_names() do
    [
      :wood_league,
      :iron_league,
      :bronze_league,
      :silver_league,
      :gold_league,
      :platinum_league,
      :expert_league,
      :master_league,
      :lord_league,
      :king_league
    ]
  end
  ```

- Tournaments depend on `Leaderboards.get_next_reset_date(schedule)` for determining when events should fire
- Configuration is pulled from `Application.get_env(:zombies_game, __MODULE__)` - a **static config** that must be manually maintained

**File: `lib/zombies_game/plague_race.ex` (base64-decoded)**
- Similar pattern with hardcoded metadata:
  ```elixir
  def event_metadata() do
    %{
      "stages" => [
        %{
          "stage" => 0,
          "total_level" => 5,
          "city" => "new_york",
          ...
        },
        ...
      ]
    }
  end
  ```

### 3. **The "Runs Out" Problem**

The scheduler uses **hardcoded stage/league definitions** that:
1. Are defined once at compile time
2. Have no dynamic generation mechanism
3. Rely on **manual extension** of the `default_leagues()` list
4. **Run out** when new leagues must be added

### 4. **Commits Around Failure Dates**

**Summer 2025 Failure (June-August 2025):**
- Commits focus on infrastructure and testing, not scheduler fixes
- Key commits: Endless monster mode setup, stats tracking, Nakama integration (July 2025)
- **No evidence of schedule extension** or fix

**Late 2025 Failure (October-December 2025):**
- **October 12, 2025**: Commit by **Arthur Blake**: "Fix zombie lane one off" - trivial level comparison fix, NOT addressing scheduler
- **No significant tournament scheduling changes** in this period
- The commit history shows the real issue was never fixed

### 5. **Evidence of "Just Extending the Hardcoded Schedule"**

Rather than implementing auto-scheduling:
- The codebase extends `default_leagues_names()` manually
- Each failure would require a new deployment to add more leagues to the list
- **No dynamic mechanism** to create leagues on demand
- **No scheduler that generates events programmatically**

### 6. **Why tournaments "stop firing":**

1. Player reaches the final league in the hardcoded list (`king_league`)
2. No new leagues are generated (no function for this)
3. `get_league_rankings()` and `promote_or_relegate_player()` attempt to promote players, but hit the **end of the hardcoded list**
4. The system can't create new tournaments because there's **no code to do so**
5. With no active tournaments, **lives/refills systems fail** (tied to event completion in `plague_race.ex`)

### 7. **Missing Remediation**

**Looking for PR that would have been the permanent fix:**
- No PR implementing **dynamic league generation**
- No PR implementing **auto-scheduling mechanism**
- No PR adding **configurable tournament templates**
- PRs in the logs focus on **localization, API endpoints, Nakama integration** - **not the core scheduler resilience**

### 8. **Authors Involved**

From commit history:
- **Arthur Blake** (`arthur.blake@harmonygames.co`) - Made trivial fix in Oct 2025, NOT scheduler
- Regular contributors (PERSON_5760_NAME, PERSON_2967_NAME) made improvements to **daily rewards** and **endless modes**, but **NOT** the core tournament scheduler

## CONCLUSION

**The event scheduler is "broken by design"** — it relies on a hardcoded list of tournaments that must be manually extended. When this list is exhausted, new tournaments cannot fire, and players lose the ability to earn lives/refills. This is not a regression; it's an architectural flaw that manifests as a failure after a predictable number of leagues are created.

The failures in summer 2025 and late 2025 appear to be symptom resurfacing after temporary extensions to the hardcoded list, rather than being caused by a specific regression.

WITH base AS (
  SELECT AVG(completion_rate_pct)/100.0 cr, SUM(revenue_generated_usd)*1.0/SUM(participants) rpp
  FROM LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE
  WHERE game_id='zombie_match_3d' AND status='completed'
)
SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, e.start_date, e.end_date, e.status,
       e.participants, e.completions,
       ROUND(e.participants*base.cr,0) expected_completions,
       ROUND(e.participants*base.cr,0)-e.completions lost_completions,
       e.revenue_generated_usd actual_rev,
       ROUND(e.participants*base.rpp,0) expected_rev,
       ROUND(e.participants*base.rpp - e.revenue_generated_usd,0) rev_shortfall
FROM LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE e, base
WHERE e.game_id='zombie_match_3d' AND e.status IN ('failed','degraded')
ORDER BY e.start_date

This is the strongest player-impact signal for the summer window: 46/46 reviews flagged incident_related, avg rating cratered from 3.60 to 2.30, and 1-star reviews jumped from 5 to 18. The late-2025 window, by contrast, shows NO review spike (avg rating 3.73, 0 incident-related) — meaning the recurrence was a silent revenue/engagement bleed, not a visible player-facing crisis.

I have enough for a rigorous, conservative report. Let me compile the findings.

---

## Impact Assessment: ZM3D Live-Ops Outages (Summer 2025 & Late 2025)

I explored the Snowflake warehouse (ANALYTICS, LIVE_OPS, FINANCE databases). The headline finding is important and defensible: the two outages have very different, and in places smaller, footprints than the internal narrative claims. I report what the data actually supports.

### Critical data-availability caveat (read first)
- **There is no dedicated "lives" ledger anywhere in the warehouse.** I checked `RESOURCE_FLOW_EVENTS` (only `coins`/`gems`/`bones` currencies; no lives), `RAW_GAME_EVENTS` (18 event names — session/progression/economy/ui/ad; no life_granted/lost/refill/regen), `PROGRESSION_EVENTS`, and `PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS` (no lives column). **The "lives stuck at 0/negative" and "no way to earn lives back" symptoms cannot be directly measured or player-counted from this warehouse.** Any lives-specific number would be a guess, so I do not provide one.
- The daily aggregate marts (`REVENUE_DAILY`, `DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS`, `PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS`) appear smoothed/synthetic and do NOT carry the incident signal. The real, defensible signal lives in transaction-grain (`IAP_TRANSACTIONS`), the event mart (`LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE`), and review-grain (`APP_STORE_REVIEWS`) data.

### 1. Live-ops / tournament impact (STRONGEST, most defensible signal)
Source: `LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE`. Healthy-event baseline (status='completed', 9 ZM3D events): avg completion rate **46.9%**, **$0.275 revenue/participant**. Counterfactual = participants × baseline rate.

| Event | Window | Status | Participants | Completions | Expected | **Lost completions** | Actual rev | **Rev shortfall** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EVT-0014 Plague Race | Jul 7-14 | failed | 639 | 60 | 300 | **240** | $13 | **~$163** |
| EVT-0015 Zombie Lane | Jul 14-28 | failed | 853 | 91 | 400 | **309** | $17 | **~$217** |
| EVT-0016 Plague Race | Aug 4-11 | degraded | 808 | 122 | 379 | **257** | $16 | **~$206** |
| EVT-0022 Endless Monster | Nov 10 - Dec 7 | degraded | 526 | 34 | 247 | **213** | $11 | **~$134** |

- **Summer 2025:** 2 tournaments (EVT-0014, EVT-0015) failed outright — completion rates collapsed to 9.4% and 10.7% vs ~47% normal. ~**549 lost completions**; failure note confirms "backend scheduler stopped; events not firing for 2 weeks." Direct event-revenue shortfall ~**$380**.
- **Late 2025:** EVT-0022 Endless Monster Mode ran degraded for ~4 weeks (Nov 10–Dec 7), 34 of 526 participants completed (6.5% vs ~47%), ~**213 lost completions**, failure note: "tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks." Shortfall ~**$134**.

### 2. Revenue impact (nuanced — smaller than the "35%" claim)
The `IAP_TRANSACTIONS` table comment asserts a "~35% revenue drop for 2 weeks (transaction gap Jul 12-26)." **The transaction-level data does not support this.** There was a sharp but brief dip, then recovery driven by the season pass:
- **Summer window:** Only Jul 12-13 dropped materially (txns 16-18/day and ~$45-47/day, vs ~34-40/day and ~$80/day just before). By Jul 14 it recovered and climbed. Net, the outage window ($101/active-day) was actually *higher* than the pre-baseline ($76/active-day) because the season pass launched mid-window. **A conservative read: ~$60-70 of directly attributable IAP loss on Jul 12-13, not a 2-week 35% gap.** There is no multi-day transaction gap in the data.
- **Late 2025 window:** A gradual erosion, not a cliff — daily IAP slid from ~$160/day (late Oct) to ~$112-124/day (late Nov/early Dec), roughly **15-20% lower** by end of window, consistent with the tournament scheduler being down and no offer surface. This is a real, sustained ~$30-40/day bleed but confounded with normal end-of-life decline (game was winding toward Jan 2026 shutdown).
- Ad revenue is tiny throughout (~$3-5/day) and not a material factor.

### 3. Player impact (measurable proxy: app-store reviews)
Source: `ANALYTICS.MARKETING.APP_STORE_REVIEWS` (`title_id='zombie_match_3d'`). This is the clearest distinct-affected-player signal available:
- **Summer 2025 (Jul 12-26): severe, visible crisis.** Avg rating cratered **3.60 → 2.30**; 1-star reviews jumped **5 → 18**; **46 of 46 reviews (100%) flagged `incident_related`.** Top incident topics across both windows: economy (14), progress_wipe (13), crash (10), ads (9).
- **Late 2025 (Oct 27-Dec 2): a SILENT bleed.** Avg rating held at **3.73**, only 8 one-star, and **0 incident-related reviews** — the recurrence was invisible to players in the storefront even though tournaments were broken. This is a meaningful distinction: summer = loud reputational damage; late-2025 = quiet monetization erosion.

### 4. Engagement impact
Not visible in the warehouse. DAU, sessions, level attempts/completions, and D1 retention in `DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS` and `PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS` show **no drop** during either window (summer DAU was even higher, ~5,109 vs ~3,537 baseline). These aggregate marts are smoothed and do not reflect the incidents; I report no engagement crater because the data doesn't show one. Distinct affected-player counts for lives/engagement cannot be derived (see caveat).

### Bottom line (conservative)
- **Directly attributable, defensible revenue loss is modest — on the order of low-to-mid hundreds of dollars per window**, not thousands: Summer ≈ $380 (events) + ~$60-70 (Jul 12-13 IAP dip); Late-2025 ≈ $134 (events) plus a sustained ~15-20% IAP softness that is partly organic decline. ZM3D was a low-revenue title (~$400/day peak, ~$33.4K lifetime).
- **The largest quantifiable player harm is in live-ops:** ~549 lost tournament completions in summer, ~213 in late 2025, and a 100%-incident-related storefront review spike in summer (rating 3.60→2.30).
- **The "35% two-week revenue gap" and the lives-specific symptoms are not supported by / not present in the warehouse.** Flag this explicitly — the narrative overstates revenue impact and the warehouse lacks a lives event stream to confirm the lives symptoms.

### Reproducibility — tables/columns used
- `LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE` (event_name, start/end_date, participants, completions, completion_rate_pct, revenue_generated_usd, status, failure_note) — event impact + counterfactual.
- `ANALYTICS.MONETIZATION.IAP_TRANSACTIONS` (date, game_id, price_usd, is_subscription) — transaction-grain revenue series (source of truth for IAP).
- `ANALYTICS.MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY` (date, iap/ad/total_revenue_usd) — cross-check (smoothed).
- `ANALYTICS.MARKETING.APP_STORE_REVIEWS` (review_date, rating, incident_related, topic_bucket) — player-impact proxy.
- `ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS` and `PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS` — engagement (showed no signal).
- Windows used: Summer baseline Jun 28-Jul 11, outage Jul 12-26; Late baseline Oct 13-26, outage Oct 27-Dec 2. All queries were read-only (SELECT); no data modified.

The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content \\u2014 Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode \\u2014 and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12\\u201326, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially \\u2014 on the order of 30% across the outage \\u2014 as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System \\u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem.

No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System \u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem.

input.title: Live-Ops scheduler resilience — implement July-2025 postmortem remediation (never built; outage recurred Oct–Dec 2025)
input.description:
## Why this ticket exists

The Live-Ops Event Engine scheduler is a **single point of failure by design**, and the remediation promised after the **July 2025 outage was never turned into tracked work and never built**. The same failure mode **recurred in Oct–Dec 2025**. This ticket exists so that remediation stops falling through the cracks.

Owners: **Douglas** (backend/scheduler) and **Arthur/Blake** will own the actual fix. This ticket is for tracking and scoping — do not treat it as closed until the items below are shipped or explicitly de-scoped.

## Root cause (design, not a one-off regression)

Per the postmortem [Live-Ops Event Engine](https://harmonygames.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/page_live_ops_engine):
- One active scheduler process, **no hot standby** → if it stalls, everything it drives goes dark.
- **Life regeneration runs on the same 60s tick loop as event firing**, so a single stall takes down two player-facing systems at once (events stop firing AND lives stop regenerating).
- Operationally, every prod deploy breaks auto-scheduling; it has been kept alive by Douglas manually rescheduling and Norman manually triggering events. That is a workaround, not a fix.

This is architectural. The Oct–Dec 2025 recurrence is the same unmitigated single point of failure resurfacing, not a new bug.

## Remediation items (verbatim from the July 2025 postmortem — none were ticketed or built)

1. **Heartbeat + external watchdog** that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
2. **Decouple life regeneration from event firing** so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
3. **Leader election** so a second process can take over the tick loop (removes the single point of failure).
4. **Lives-regeneration reconciler** that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
5. **Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue** so drift is visible on the same screen.

Verified missing: a Linear search for watchdog/heartbeat/decouple/leader-election/reconciler returned **zero** issues. ENG-2238 (scheduler rule changes) was done in May 2025 and predates the outage; ENG-2240 (liveops calendar web UI) was **cancelled** on 2025-11-05 and was never one of these five items.

## Verified impact (warehouse source of truth: LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE, ANALYTICS.MARKETING.APP_STORE_REVIEWS)

- **Summer 2025:** Plague Race (Jul 7–14) and Zombie Lane (Jul 14–28) both `status=failed`; completion collapsed from a ~40–61% norm to **9%** and **11%**; failure_note = "backend scheduler stopped; events not firing for 2 weeks." ~**549 lost tournament completions**. App-store rating **3.60 → 2.30**, one-star reviews **5 → 18**, and **46/46 (100%) reviews incident-related** — a loud, visible player crisis.
- **Late 2025 (recurrence):** Endless Monster Mode (Nov 10–Dec 7) `status=degraded`, **7%** completion; failure_note = "tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks." ~**213 lost completions**. **0 incident-related reviews** — a silent monetization/engagement bleed rather than a visible crisis.
- Note on revenue: the postmortem's "~30% revenue drop" is not reproducible from transaction-grain warehouse data (a season-pass launch buoyed total IAP mid-window in summer; late-2025 shows a sustained ~15–20% IAP softness confounded with organic end-of-life decline). The clearest, defensible harm is in the live-ops layer (completion collapse + lost completions) and the summer storefront reputation hit.
- The warehouse has **no lives event ledger**, so lives-specific affected-player counts cannot be derived from it; player harm on lives is evidenced by support tickets and the open bugs below.

## Related open tickets (players not getting lives — currently floating unattached)

- **ZOM-667** — "Lives regen syncing issues" (P1, Todo, assignee Douglas) — refill/inventory not syncing.
- **ENG-2400** — "Lives are not generating for some real players" (P1, Bugs, assignee Blake) — lives not regenerating after long absence (Domino Delights; same shared engine).

Remediation item #2 (decouple lives from the tick loop) and #4 (lives reconciler) directly address the class of failure these two tickets report.

## Scope note

Config and scheduling were intentionally **not** touched during this investigation. This ticket is scoping/tracking for Douglas + Arthur to own the fix.
