input.body:
The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D ("Puzzles vs Zombies" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content — Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode — and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12–26, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially — on the order of 30% across the outage — as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System — Design & Incident Postmortem.

This came back. The same scheduler failure mode recurred in Oct–Dec 2025. As of this update, none of the July 2025 remediation items above were ever turned into tracked work or built. Recurrence, root-cause confirmation, remediation status, and verified impact are documented below. Tracking ticket: ENG-2438.

Update — 2026-04-26: recurrence (Oct–Dec 2025) & remediation status

The failure recurred

The scheduler failure resurfaced in late 2025. It was first raised in the incidents channel on Oct 27, 2025 (Win & Collect not unlocking; only a subset of weekend events firing) and was still being escalated on Nov 30 – Dec 2, 2025 ("tournaments haven't restarted for weeks"). In the warehouse, Endless Monster Mode (Nov 10 – Dec 7, 2025) is recorded with status=degraded and the failure note "tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks" — completion collapsed to 7% (34 of 526 participants) versus a ~40–61% norm.

Root cause is unchanged — this is the same single point of failure, not a new regression

The recurrence is the same architectural fault this page already warns about: one scheduler process, no hot standby, and life regeneration coupled to event firing on the same tick loop. The operational reality confirmed in the incidents channel is that every production deployment breaks auto-scheduling, after which the scheduler has been kept alive only by Douglas manually rescheduling and Norman manually triggering events. That is a standing workaround, not a fix — the system has been one missed manual step away from another outage the entire time.

Remediation status: none of the July 2025 action items were built

A review of Linear found no tickets for any of the five July 2025 remediation items (heartbeat/watchdog, decouple lives from event firing, leader election, lives-regeneration reconciler, last-tick dashboard). For the avoidance of doubt on adjacent tickets: ENG-2238 ("Change event scheduler rules") was completed in May 2025 and predates the outage; ENG-2240 ("Web interface for the liveops calendar") was cancelled on 2025-11-05 and was never one of the five items. The remediation was therefore never tracked and never built. It is now captured in ENG-2438, owned by Douglas and Arthur.

Open "players not getting lives" tickets (now linked)

  • ZOM-667 — "Lives regen syncing issues" (P1, Todo, Douglas) — refill/inventory not syncing; lives revert to a stale value.
  • ENG-2400 — "Lives are not generating for some real players" (P1, Bugs, Blake) — lives not regenerating after a long absence (Domino Delights; same shared engine).

Both are now cross-linked to ENG-2438. Remediation items #2 (decouple lives from the tick loop) and #4 (lives reconciler) directly address the class of failure they report.

Verified impact (warehouse source of truth)

From LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE and ANALYTICS.MARKETING.APP_STORE_REVIEWS:

WindowEvent(s)StatusCompletion rate~Lost completionsStorefront signal
Summer 2025 (Jul)Plague Race (Jul 7–14), Zombie Lane (Jul 14–28)failed / failed9% and 11% (norm ~40–61%)~549Rating 3.60→2.30; 1-star 5→18; 46/46 reviews (100%) incident-related
Late 2025 (Nov–Dec)Endless Monster Mode (Nov 10–Dec 7)degraded7% (norm ~40–61%)~2130 incident-related reviews — a silent bleed, not a visible crisis

Correction on the "~30%" figure. The clearest, reproducible harm sits in the live-ops layer (completion collapse and ~549 / ~213 lost tournament completions) and, in summer, a sharp storefront reputation hit. The "~30% revenue drop" stated for July 2025 could not be reproduced from transaction-grain warehouse data: total IAP in the summer window was buoyed by a season-pass launch mid-outage, and the late-2025 window shows a sustained ~15–20% IAP softness that is confounded with the game's organic end-of-life decline. Separately, the warehouse has no lives event ledger, so lives-specific affected-player counts cannot be derived from it — the lives harm is evidenced by support tickets and the open bugs above, not by a warehouse count.

Scope of this update

No live event config or scheduling was touched during this investigation. This update is the record; ENG-2438 is the tracking; Douglas and Arthur own the actual fix.

The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D ("Puzzles vs Zombies" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content \u2014 Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode \u2014 and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12\u201326, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially \u2014 on the order of 30% across the outage \u2014 as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

*1. It's the same failure, and it's by design — not a new regression.*
The Live-Ops Event Engine runs on a single scheduler process with no hot standby, and life regeneration is coupled to event firing on the *same* 60s tick loop. Operationally, every prod deploy breaks auto-scheduling and it's been kept alive only by Douglas manually rescheduling / Norman manually triggering. That's the July 2025 outage and the Oct–Dec 2025 recurrence — same root cause, different date. The postmortem already warned this was a single point of failure.

The July 2025 postmortem listed 5 fixes (watchdog/heartbeat, decouple lives from event firing, leader election, lives reconciler, last-tick dashboard). Linear has *zero* tickets for any of them. ENG-2238 (scheduler rules) predates the outage; ENG-2240 (calendar web UI) was cancelled Nov 5. So the follow-up work genuinely never happened.

*What I've set up (tracking only — no config/scheduling touched):*
• New ticket *ENG-2438* — "Live-Ops scheduler resilience — implement July-2025 postmortem remediation (never built; recurred Oct–Dec 2025)." Assigned Douglas; Arthur co-owns.

*Ownership:* Douglas + Arthur own the actual fix. I deliberately did not touch any live event config or the scheduler — this is just the picture and the tracking.

**It's the same failure both times, and it's broken by design — not a fresh regression.** The Live-Ops Event Engine runs on a *single* scheduler process with no hot standby, and — critically — player life regeneration is deliberately coupled to event firing on the *same* 60-second tick loop. So when the scheduler stalls, tournaments stop firing **and** lives stop regenerating at the same moment. That's exactly what the July 2025 postmortem already documented as a "single point of failure." The late-2025 recurrence is that same unmitigated fault resurfacing. The operational reality confirmed in Slack: **every prod deploy breaks auto-scheduling**, and it's only been held together by Douglas manually rescheduling and Norman manually triggering events. Your instinct was right — the underlying problem was never fixed; it was worked around.

**The follow-up work genuinely never happened.** The July 2025 postmortem listed five remediation items (watchdog/heartbeat, decouple lives from event firing, leader election, lives reconciler, last-tick dashboard). A Linear sweep found **zero** tickets for any of them. The two adjacent tickets are red herrings: ENG-2238 (scheduler rules) was done in May 2025, *before* the outage; ENG-2240 (calendar web UI) was **cancelled Nov 5, 2025** and wasn't one of the five anyway.

**Verified impact (warehouse, not vibes):**
- **Summer 2025** — Plague Race and Zombie Lane both `status=failed`, completion collapsed from a ~40–61% norm to **9%/11%** (~549 lost completions); the failure note literally reads *"backend scheduler stopped; events not firing for 2 weeks."* App-store rating **3.60→2.30**, one-star **5→18**, **46/46 reviews (100%) incident-related** — a loud, visible crisis.
- **Late 2025** — Endless Monster Mode `degraded`, **7%** completion (~213 lost completions), note *"tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks."* But **0 incident-related reviews** — a silent bleed.
- One correction worth flagging: the postmortem's headline **"~30% revenue drop" is not reproducible** from transaction-grain data (summer IAP was buoyed by a season-pass launch mid-outage; late-2025 softness is ~15–20% but confounded with the game's end-of-life decline). And there's **no lives ledger in the warehouse**, so lives-specific player counts can't be derived — that harm lives in support tickets/bugs.

1. **Created ENG-2438** — "Live-Ops scheduler resilience — implement July-2025 postmortem remediation (never built; outage recurred Oct–Dec 2025)." 4. **Posted a status in #live-incidents** summarizing all of the above, with Douglas + Arthur named as owners of the fix and an explicit note that no config/scheduling was touched.

Douglas and Arthur now own the actual fix — the picture and the tracking are straight, and the never-built remediation is undeniable and on the record.
